caption: Start of motorway
colour: Blue background, white motorway symbol (a carriageway passing under a bridge), thin white border
explanation: Marks where you enter a motorway and motorway regulations begin (national speed limit, no stopping on the carriageway, keep-left lane discipline). Motorways must not be used by learner motorcyclists, mopeds and motorcycles under 50cc, cyclists, pedestrians, animals, or vehicles that cannot reach 25mph — so as a CBT rider you cannot ride past this sign.
mnemonic: Blue plate, white ‘bridge-over-a-road’ motorway symbol and no red line = motorway STARTS here. (The same sign with a red slash through it means it ends.)
notes: TSRGD diagram 2901 'Start of motorway regulations, including the national speed limit'. Official OGL SVG on Commons (UK traffic sign 2901.svg): background/border motorway blue #0079c1, symbol/lettering white #ffffff, NO red and NO diagonal element. The white symbol is a dual carriageway passing under a bridge.

caption: End of motorway
colour: Blue background, white motorway symbol with a single red diagonal bar struck through it
explanation: Tells you that you are leaving the motorway and motorway regulations no longer apply from the point shown; expect a change of speed limit (often lower) and ordinary road conditions — junctions, slower traffic, cyclists, pedestrians and learners. Slow down and be ready for the road to behave like a normal road.
mnemonic: Same blue plate and white motorway symbol as ‘start’, but now a RED diagonal bar strikes through it = motorway rules ENDED.
notes: TSRGD diagram 2931 'End of motorway regulations, including the national speed limit'. Official OGL SVG on Commons (UK traffic sign 2931.svg): only colours present are blue #0079c1 (background), white #ffffff (border + motorway symbol) and exactly one red element #ec1d24 (the diagonal bar). NOT the 2902.x direction-to-motorway series.

caption: Motorway countdown markers
colour: Tall blue plates with a white border; three, then two, then one white diagonal (sloping) bars — counting down to the exit
explanation: On a motorway these tall blue markers count you down to the exit: three bars at 300 yards, two at 200 yards, one at 100 yards from the start of the deceleration (slip) lane. Check your mirrors, signal left in good time and be settled in the left-hand lane before the first (three-bar) marker.
mnemonic: Blue plates with white slashes counting down 3-2-1 to the exit (three slashes = 300 yards away; one slash = 100 yards, exit next).
notes: Composite: drawn in-app as a single three-plate card (3/2/1 diagonal bars) — clearer than three separate official SVGs (TSRGD 823/824/825, '-B-L'/'-B-R' for left/right exits). Blue panel #01619e, white bars rotated ~27°, black+white rounded borders. Blue = motorway (green on primary routes; a separate white-with-red version 789 is used at level crossings).

caption: Motorway junction ahead
colour: Large blue sign, white lettering, arrows and border; the junction number is white on a small black patch
explanation: A large blue advance direction sign warns of a motorway junction ahead, usually posted one mile and again half a mile before the exit. It shows the junction number, the destinations and route numbers, and downward arrows meaning ‘get in lane’ (the left-hand lane usually leads somewhere different). Read it early and move into the correct lane in good time.
mnemonic: Big BLUE board, small BLACK box holding the junction number (e.g. ‘J11’) and white DOWNWARD arrows = motorway junction ahead, get in lane.
searchTerms: one mile half mile exit sign
notes: Composite: drawn in-app. Advance direction signs are bespoke per-junction assemblies (junction number, destinations, route numbers, distance, lane arrows) with no single fixed TSRGD diagram — like the existing route-confirmation-sign composite. Highway Code: most motorway signs are blue with white legend; junction number on a black patch; downward arrows mean 'get in lane'.

caption: Motorway route confirmatory sign
colour: Blue background, white lettering and border; motorway number at the top, destinations listed with their distances in miles
explanation: Sited after most motorway junctions, this blue sign confirms the motorway number (e.g. M1) and lists the main destinations ahead with their distances in miles, so you know you are on the right road. Colour codes the road class: blue = motorway, green = primary route, white = non-primary route.
mnemonic: Blue panel + M-number on top + town names with miles = you’re still on the motorway, going the right way.
notes: Composite: drawn in-app (per-route assembly, TSRGD diagram 2911 — no clean whole-sign SVG on Commons). Blue panel, white legend, no arrows: motorway number on top, then destinations with right-aligned mile distances. Distinct from the GREEN primary-route and WHITE non-primary confirmatory signs.

caption: Motorway service area sign
colour: Blue panel, white border, white facility symbols; the petrol-pump symbol is green. A separate upper panel carries the service name
explanation: About half a mile before motorway services, this blue sign names the service area and shows white symbols for the facilities available (fuel, refreshments, toilets, information, accommodation) plus the petrol price by a green pump symbol. Use it to decide whether to pull in for a break.
mnemonic: Motorway blue + white facility symbols (cup, knife & fork, bed) and one splash of colour — a GREEN petrol pump = services this way.
searchTerms: petrol knife and fork bed sign
notes: Composite: drawn in-app. Diagram 2919.1 'Motorway service area ahead' (DfT working drawing P2919.1) is a per-site assembly with no whole-sign SVG on Commons. Drawing Note 4 fixes the main panel: Background BLUE, Legend/Border/Symbols WHITE, Pump GREEN on white tile. The upper operator panel's colours are variable (Note 7) — keep it neutral, not a fixed white/red board. Brown ground would be a tourist-facilities sign, not this.

caption: Variable mandatory speed limit
colour: Overhead gantry signal: dark panel with a white speed number inside a red ring
explanation: On a smart motorway, a speed shown inside a red ring on the gantry is a mandatory, legally enforceable limit, monitored by cameras and varied to manage congestion and incidents — slow to it straight away. The same number with NO red ring is only advisory.
mnemonic: Red ring round the number = it’s the LAW, not a suggestion (no ring = just advice).
searchTerms: speed in a red circle overhead
what does a red ring speed mean
notes: Composite, drawn in-app: teaches the MODERN smart-motorway gantry display (white speed number in a true RED RING on a dark panel) per gov.uk Know Your Traffic Signs. Do NOT import the OGL 'UK Overhead Matrix Signal - Speed Limit 50.svg' — it renders the OLD amber dot-matrix aspect with no red ring. Red ring ~#C8102E, white number, near-black panel.

caption: Red X — lane closed
colour: Overhead gantry signal: dark panel showing a solid red cross (red X) with flashing red lights
explanation: A red X with flashing red lights above a lane means that lane is closed (a broken-down vehicle, debris, workers or a hazard ahead): move out of that lane before the signal and do not drive past it in that lane. It is an offence enforced by camera — a fixed penalty of up to £100 and 3 penalty points.
mnemonic: Red X = lane crossed out — get out of it before the gantry, never drive under the X.
searchTerms: can I drive under a red x
notes: Composite, drawn in-app — based on the existing 'lane-control-signal' red-X composite, plus small red corner lamps for the flashing red lights. Distinct teaching value from lane-control-signal: the flashing lamps and the legal 'MUST NOT / £100 + 3 points, camera-enforced' on a live running lane (Highway Code rule 258, National Highways Red X campaign). No single OGL SVG of the whole flashing signal.

caption: Amber flashing signal
colour: Dark matrix signal with amber lamps flashing in the corners; centre shows an amber advisory speed (no red ring) or a lane-change arrow
explanation: Amber lights flashing in pairs (top to bottom) warn of a hazard ahead; the panel may show an advisory speed (no red ring) or a diagonal arrow telling you to change lane. Slow down and follow it, and speed up again only after a non-flashing signal or a sign showing ‘END’ or the national speed limit — and only when it is safe.
mnemonic: Amber flashing, amber number with NO red ring = advice, not the law — ease off.
notes: Composite, drawn in-app. Highway Code rule 257 / gov.uk KYTS: each signal has 2 pairs of amber lights that flash top to bottom; an amber speed NOT in a red circle is advisory (contrast the mandatory red-ring limit and the red-flashing closed-lane X). Amber lamps + amber number/arrow, NO red anywhere.

caption: End of restriction
colour: Overhead matrix signal: a dark lamp grid with the word END picked out in lit amber lamps
explanation: On a motorway gantry or matrix signal, END (like a national speed limit sign) cancels the previous temporary speed limit, lane restriction or hazard warning. You may return to the normal speed limit and use any lane again once you have passed it and are sure it is safe.
mnemonic: Amber END glowing on the dark lamp grid: the restriction’s lifted, you’re back to normal.
notes: Official OGL SVG (UK Overhead Matrix Signal - End.svg, NMCS2 matrix aspect): END in lit amber lamps #F7931D, unlit lamps #4C4C4C, transparent backing (reads as a dark lamp grid on the plate). It's an electronic matrix signal, so the 'motorway signs are blue' rule does not apply. No TSRGD diagram (matrix indicators are NMCS drawings).
